boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct FSU study environments, from quiet reading rooms and solo carrels to reservable collaboration rooms and technology-equipped workspaces.

cards.title: Settle Into the Bradley Reading Room
cards.subtitle: A controlled-access quiet room for graduate students and faculty
cards.notes: Submit the access form at least two days ahead, then bring your activated FSU card and plan on silent, independent work.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level Strozier retreat dedicated to quiet graduate and faculty research.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries identifies the Bradley Reading Room as a quiet independent-study space for graduate students and faculty, prohibits talking and group work, and requires an access form with 24–48 hours for card activation.
cards.source_title: Bradley Reading Room (Quiet Area) | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Strozier Library's ground floor. Limited to FSU graduate students and faculty; submit the access form and allow 24–48 hours for card activation.

cards.entity_name: Dr. Mary Lou Norwood Reading Room
cards.title: Read Quietly in the Norwood Room
cards.subtitle: Round-table study inside Strozier's second-floor archives setting
cards.notes: Check that the room is not reserved for an event, then use its large tables for quiet reading during Strozier's open hours.
cards.short_summary: A named archival reading room that doubles as a quiet study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Special Collections states that the Dr. Mary Lou Norwood Reading Room is on Strozier Library's second floor and is available for quiet study during Strozier's open hours unless reserved for a meeting or event.
cards.source_title: Visit Special Collections and Archives | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use is tied to Strozier Library's open hours, and the room may be unavailable when reserved for a meeting or event.

cards.title: Work Solo Behind a Door
cards.subtitle: First-come individual rooms on Strozier's quiet second floor
cards.notes: Ask the Scholar Support Desk for a key; the four-hour loan suits a focused work block, with renewal only if demand permits.
cards.short_summary: Twenty single-seat rooms designed for focused individual work in Strozier.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries says rooms 2041–2060 seat one person, are available to FSU undergraduate and graduate students and faculty, use a four-hour key loan, and are first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable online. Request a key at Strozier's Scholar Support Desk; rooms are individual-only with a four-hour loan period.

cards.title: Take the Group Work Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Small collaboration rooms on a designated quiet floor
cards.notes: Reserve a room before meeting and keep conversation contained; each space is sized for a small team of two to four people.
cards.short_summary: Compact third-floor rooms for collaborative sessions without using an open table.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries lists Strozier Group Study Rooms 331–342 as spaces seating two to four people, available to all eligible library users through its room-use system, and located on a quiet floor.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms and Spaces | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the FSU Libraries room system. These rooms seat two to four and sit on a quiet floor; unaffiliated individuals and outside groups cannot book library space.

cards.title: Find a Solo Room at Dirac
cards.subtitle: Individual workspaces inside FSU's science library
cards.notes: Choose this option for work that benefits from a closed room, and consult the library booking page before walking to Dirac.
cards.short_summary: Reservable single-person rooms within the STEM-focused Dirac Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries lists Individual Study Rooms 103H–307H at Dirac Science Library as single-seat spaces available to all eligible library users through its room-use system.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms and Spaces | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Consult the FSU Libraries room-use system before arrival. Library booking is unavailable to unaffiliated individuals, community groups, and outside organizations.

cards.title: Book a Four-Person Dirac Room
cards.subtitle: Third-floor rooms for small-team problem solving
cards.notes: Reserve up to three days ahead and retain the confirmation email; vacant rooms may be used by groups without a reservation.
cards.short_summary: Three small rooms with clear advance-booking and daily-use limits.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries says Dirac rooms 303–305 hold up to four people, may be reserved by FSU students, faculty, and staff for up to four hours daily, and open reservations three days ahead.
cards.access_notes: FSU students, faculty, and staff may reserve up to four hours per day and up to three days ahead. Keep the confirmation email available.

cards.title: Combine Study Time With Academic Support
cards.subtitle: Study rooms, computer labs, and printers in William Johnston Building
cards.notes: Bring assignments that need a computer or printer, and check Campus Connect if you also want an Academic Center for Excellence appointment.
cards.short_summary: A practical academic workspace pairing study infrastructure with ACE support.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Student Affairs states that students are welcome to use the WJB Learning Studio's study rooms, computer labs, and printers and directs students to Campus Connect for appointment times.
cards.source_title: Finals Study Spots | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open to FSU students during posted Learning Studio hours. Check Campus Connect for ACE appointment availability and Student Affairs for current operating hours.

cards.title: Move a Project Into the Innovation Hub
cards.subtitle: Phone booths, a huddle room, and collaborative project space
cards.notes: Reserve a phone booth for solo calls or the huddle room for teamwork, then consult the floor plan for other space capacities.
cards.short_summary: A flexible project environment with bookable rooms and collaborative technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The FSU Innovation Hub says students can reserve two small phone-booth study rooms and one group huddle room and provides a floor plan showing capacities for additional spaces.
cards.access_notes: Student reservations are available through the Hub's reservation page. The Hub closes during semester breaks and holidays; verify current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Use a Union Room Between Commitments
cards.subtitle: Six numbered study rooms inside the FSU Student Union
cards.notes: Look for rooms 1281, 1282, 1283, 2211, 2212, 2214 and confirm current building and room hours before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Six clearly identified rooms in a central campus building with separate access hours.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Student Affairs identifies Student Union study rooms 1281, 1282, 1283, 2211, 2212, and 2214 and distinguishes the rooms' operating times from general building-access hours.
cards.source_title: Finals Study Spots | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Student access follows posted Union building hours, while study rooms may follow a separate schedule. Verify the current Student Affairs listing before visiting.

cards.title: Check Out a Room at Thagard
cards.subtitle: Twenty-five private and group rooms managed by CARE
cards.notes: Choose a private or group room, check it out through CARE, and shape the session around the stated two-hour maximum.
cards.short_summary: A large collection of checkout-based rooms supporting solo and collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Student Affairs states that CARE at Thagard provides 25 private and group study rooms and permits students to check out a room for a maximum of two hours.
cards.source_title: Finals Study Spots | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: For FSU student use through CARE. Room checkout is limited to two hours; verify current Thagard operating hours before arrival.
